# Engraving recipe

Copper intaglio, drawn live. A burin plows a groove into polished copper, a proof lifts off, and the figure grows on paper in passes while the loupe backs away. Capitals get cut letter by letter, one part is scribed into a magnifying roundel that flies to the margin on a leader, and hand-laid washes close the plate.

## Look

One sheet, one unbroken take: cut on copper, proof, figure, lettering, magnified detail, colour, finished plate. Every mark is ink sitting in a groove.

Three laws for every frame:
1. Tone is line density. Bare paper is light. One set of parallel lines gives half-tone, a second set crossing it gives shadow, a third set making lozenges gives the deepest dark. Never a grey fill in the ink.
2. Lines swell and taper. The burin starts thin, digs in mid-run, lifts out to a point. Widen where the form turns away from the light; let the line vanish where the form faces it. Cut contours in several runs and thin them where one run hands to the next. Constant width looks like a pen or vector: reject it.
3. Colour is last and by hand. Transparent watercolour is laid one region at a time on top of the completed black print. It spills over the lines and pools at its edge. Ink stays on top. A film can stay monochrome a long time; when colour comes, it is the event.

Not a woodcut (solid black, pale gouges), not a pen sketch (loose, broken strokes), not an engineering drawing, not a sepia photo, not interface motion. Nothing fades or slides in. Lines are cut, letters are cut or written, colour blooms, sheets are peeled or laid down.

## Surfaces

- Paper: 1920x1080 world units of laid paper. Paint the texture once (fine grain, faint low-frequency mottling, laid lines every 4 px, chain lines every 72 px); it zooms with the camera.
- Plate mark: pressed rectangle 70,44 to 1850,1036. Bevel 5 px, dark on top and left walls, light on bottom and right. Inside, a 5% film of plate tone.
- Ruled border: 100,72 to 1820,1008. A 2.4 px rule with a 0.8 px hairline 9 px inside it.
- Narration: a paper slip at bottom centre over the lower border, soft static shadow.
- Roundel: double ring (2.4 px and 0.9 px), burnished paper disc. Author the content at radius 500 local units and scale it in, so nothing shimmers.
- Leader: 0.95 px hairline, running from a dot on the part out to the rim. Route it through a waypoint around the figure, never across.
- Hand colour sits under the ink. Paint each region's sheet once: 3.5 px spill past the line, 2 px misregister, a darker tide-line at the wet edge, uneven pigment. It blooms from the brush touch with a ragged front, opacity 0.55-0.72.

## Ink and line rules

- Ink: a single warm near-black.
- Width ratios: outlines heaviest, x0.64 on the lit side to x1.36 on the shadow side, pinched to 45% at each burin handover (about every 110 px). First hatch family: 0.18 px hair up to about 1.9 px. Crossing family x0.78. Third family x0.6.
- Spacing: about 3 px on a 400 px figure (1/130 to 1/180 of its height; tighter turns grey). Later families x1.1 and x1.25.
- Swell law per hatch line: width x (0.2 + 0.8*sin(pi u)^0.7). Taper the first and last 22%. Add 0.35 px wobble so it reads cut, not plotted.
- Families switch on by tone (0-1 scale) at 0.14, 0.5, 0.78.
- Light: one source, upper left, whole film. Derive tone from geometry, never from texture: analytic sphere for a fruit or head, cylinder for a stem or limb, leaf lit on its upper half and dark along the fold.
- Hatch follows the form: parabola-bent lines wrap a sphere, lines run along a stem's axis, lines follow a leaf's lateral veins.
- Occlusion is geometric. Lines stop at shapes in front.

## Copper opening

Polished warm plate, dark room falling off at the corners. Reflect a four-pane window softly: blur once, then only translate it at 0.09x parallax. Add faint light scratches of the traced design.

- Groove: dark trough, lit burr on the light side, soft shadow on the far side.
- Burin: lozenge steel shaft with bevelled face, brass ferrule, mushroom wooden handle, soft cast shadow. It trails the cut, turned 13 degrees off the line so the fresh groove stays visible.
- Swarf: a thin copper ribbon curling ahead of the point, opening from 0.6 to 3.2 turns as the cut lengthens.
- The copper scene never carries text.

## Palette

- `--latar` = paper. `--teks` = ink: all lines, rules, letters. Plate tone, bevel and vignette are mixes of these two.
- Dark brand: light lines on dark paper, a white-line engraving. Still lines, no fills.
- `--utama`: the one strong pigment, washed on the part that matters (in the example the fruit rind and its roundel).
- `--aksen`: the second, muted pigment (leaves). The calyx is 62% `--aksen` mixed with `--utama`.
- Washes: transparent, after the print, never over lettering, rules, or paper outside the figure. Colour either the whole subject in one beat, or just the part under discussion.
- `--latar-2`: narration slip. `--teks-redup`: secondary credits. Lettering stays ink, so `--utama-di-latar` and `--aksen-di-latar` go unused.
- Fixed in all brands: the opening workshop (copper from deep brown to warm orange, pale burr, near-black trough, steel, brass, wood).
- Example values: paper `#e2d3b4` (measures `#dbcbab` under the vignette), ink `#1c1510`, copper `#94502c` to `#4e220e`, washes madder-aubergine and sage green.

## Type

- `--font-judul`: Roman capitals, Playfair Display 700. Title 64 px, tracking 0.16 em, ends with a full stop. Labels 24 px, tracking 0.14 em ("GBR. 1 · KELOPAK BINTANG"). Scientific names in Playfair Display 400 italic: 38 px under the title, 34 px under a label.
- `--font-isi`: the hand. Cormorant Garamond 500 italic. Roundel notes 42 px, line height 1.1, balanced across two lines, never shrunk. Narration slip 46 px.
- No brand fonts? Capitals in a high-contrast or bookish roman (Playfair Display, Libre Baskerville, IM Fell English); hand in Cormorant Garamond italic.
- Capitals are cut glyph by glyph. Wipe each glyph in from the left over 1.5 glyph-steps, where step = duration / (letters + 2). Title takes 0.9 s, label 0.6 s.
- Notes are written in one left-to-right stroke with a soft wet edge 0.7 em wide, 0.5-0.6 s per line. Nothing fades in. Keep a note up for characters / 12 + 1 s.
- Keep labels at 24 px or more, notes and narration at 40 px or more (at 1920 wide). Real plate lettering of 15-20 px disappears on a phone.

## Timing

Order of cutting drives the animation. Sequence: outline, then first hatching sweeping across each form, then crossing, then darks. Burin speed stays even, so each stroke's window scales with its length. Run up to 16 contours, 70 hatch lines and 90 dark lines at once. A full build lasts about 4 s; a single long stroke may be followed by the camera.

The 15 s example:
- Copper: first contour 0-2.0 s (pre-cut 2.2 s, so no frame is empty). Burin lifts 2.0-2.35 s.
- Proof peel 2.5-3.2 s: a diagonal fold travels from bottom right, leaving a 380 px curled flap with dark crease and bright roll, its shadow on the copper.
- Paper: outlines 2.6-4.6, hatching 3.3-5.5, crossing 4.4-6.2, darks 5.0-6.9, border ruled 3.0-5.6.
- Title cut at 6.25 s, Latin name at 6.7 s. The full plate holds about 2 s.
- Then: push-in 1.0 s, ring scribed 0.4 s, burnished 0.3 s, roundel content cut 1.35 s, flight 1.1 s, labels cut on landing, washes blooming 1.0-1.1 s each starting 0.15-0.3 s apart, final still hold 2 s.

Eases: camera cubic in-out with log zoom. Roundel flight cubic in-out along an arc rising 30 px, radius growing log-linearly from 48 to 120 px. Wash front 1 - (1 - p)^2.2 with a ragged edge. Strokes and letters linear.
Slip: drops in over 0.25 s (8 px, power2.out), lifts out over 0.2 s.

## Camera

A loupe over a sheet: focus point in world units, scale, slight rotation. Zoom interpolates in log space; on big zooms the pan follows 1/z so the target holds still.

- Ride the burin's point at 3.6x, rotation -0.05 to -0.01 rad. One point of attention, a making: first mark, signature, promise being written.
- Pull out 3.3x to 1x over 3 s, log zoom. The line belonged to something bigger: scale reveal, context, the whole plan.
- Push to a part, 1x to 3x in 1 s, then return to 1x riding with its roundel. Where, then what: hidden detail, mechanism, ingredient.
- Locked frame, or a breathing push of 2% at most. The plate as document: reading time, colour arriving, the ending.
- Pan across the sheet at reading zoom. Labels taken in sequence: parts list, coastline, recipe steps.
- Raking view across the copper. Groove as depth: cost of craft, a handmade process.

Framing: keep the subject within the plate mark and push labels and roundels out to the margins. Put consecutive details on one side so a push-in never crops a fresh note. Transitions come only from printmaking: proof peeled, tissue guard laid over, a region burnished out and re-cut, a new sheet laid on the bed. No dissolves, no wipes.

## Signature moves

- The cut: burin mid-stroke on copper, swarf curling ahead, camera on the point. Use for a farm logo's first line, a watchmaker scribing a dial, a teacher's first stroke, a family story's opening.
- The proof: the sheet peels off and copper becomes paper bearing the same lines. Use for a draft turning final, a bakery card printed from a founder's notebook, a sketch becoming the thumbnail, a secret out.
- Three passes: volume builds pass by pass as the loupe retreats. Use for a building from its plan, ripening fruit, a skill across three course levels, a portrait emerging in a mystery.
- Roundel: scribe a ring on one part, burnish, re-cut its content larger, fly it to the margin on a leader, cut its label on landing. Use for a mangosteen's base star, a watch movement in a repair shop, a taught stitch, a seed in biology class.
- Hand colouring: after the print, washes bloom region by region from a brush touch, one strong pigment on what matters. Use for ripe rind, one organ in an anatomy lesson, a heritage walking route, a flag on a history chart.
- Finished plate: title, roundel, labels, margin note, all locked and held. Use for a museum label, a farm's seasonal calendar, a channel end card, a class certificate.
- States of the plate: burnish a region out and re-cut it differently. Use for renovation before/after, a redesigned product, old and new timetables, a character changed by the story.
- Natural size: pair the large engraving with a tiny figure at true scale. Use for a seed by its tree, a ring beside its enlargement, an insect, a chip beside its circuit.

## Avoid

- Pen look: swell every hatch line, pinch contours between runs, keep minimum width a hair.
- Fills: no grey or coloured fill in ink. Tone from density only; colour only as a transparent wash beneath the ink, never on lettering.
- Transparent-looking overlaps: feed the shapes in front as exclusions to both hatching and outlines.
- Per-frame full redraw: keep one canvas, extend only the strokes being cut. Paint paper and washes once into images, blur the window reflection once on a layer that only moves, hide the copper scene after the peel. A repainted full-size canvas or animated blur drops the preview frame rate.
- Raster blur on zoom: paint the ink layer at about 2.2x world resolution for zooms up to 3.5x; author roundel content large.
- Leaders hugging or crossing the figure read as part of it. Route through clear paper.
- Hard-coded black lines or cream paper: on a white brand washes still show because ink sits on top; on a dark brand the ink token goes light.

## Structures

You choose subject, details, order, opening, ending, camera path and colour. Use cases fix information order and hold times:
- Museum or shop label, 15-40 s: title and scientific name, then detail, term, note, then where to see or buy. Title holds 2.2 s or more, note chars/12 + 1 s or more, final 2 s or more.
- "One minute on ...", 30-60 s: question, name, 2-3 facts, one number, follow prompt. Number alone 2.5 s or more.
- Textbook figure, 20-45 s: figure, parts labelled one at a time, caption. Label chars/12 + 1 s or more.
- Craft heritage, 30-45 s: object, 2-3 craft details, maker and edition. Same holds.
- Map or site plan, 30-45 s: the place first, then insets, legend, and how to visit. Inset 3 s or more, legend 4 s or more.

Other shapes: states of one plate (the same view re-cut three times while a place changes); a book of plates (small plates that turn like pages, a fact apiece); a dissection (parts labelled in teaching order, colour on the taught part alone).
Openings: the finished proof burnished back down to its first line; paper at 1x with the title cut first.
Endings: plate beside its proof; natural-size figure held alone; blank sheet laid on the stack.

# Copper engraving: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.8, medium 2.6, long 3.4.

## hook

- en: the burin cuts the first contour into polished copper, the camera riding its point as swarf curls; then the proof peels off
- id: burin memotong kontur pertama di tembaga mengilap, kamera menunggangi ujungnya, serpih menggulung; lalu lembar cetak dikelupas

## problem

- en: a region of the plate is burnished out and re-cut: the flaw scraped bare, then engraved again line by line
- id: satu bagian pelat digosok hilang lalu dipahat ulang: cacatnya dikerok polos, kemudian diukir lagi garis demi garis

## fact

- en: a magnifier roundel is scribed on the part, re-cut larger and flown to the margin on a leader; its label is cut on landing
- id: lingkaran pembesar digores di bagian itu, dipahat ulang lebih besar, terbang ke margin dengan garis penunjuk; labelnya dipahat

## step

- en: one form per step, cut in three passes (outline, hatching, cross-hatching) while the camera pulls back on a log zoom
- id: satu bentuk tiap langkah, dipahat tiga lintasan (kontur, arsir, arsir silang) sambil kamera mundur perlahan

## compare

- en: two states of one plate side by side: the left as first cut, the right re-cut denser; a label cut under each
- id: dua keadaan satu pelat berdampingan: kiri potongan pertama, kanan dipahat ulang lebih rapat; label dipahat di bawahnya

## number

- en: the figure cut glyph by glyph in roman capitals beside a tiny natural-size engraving, held alone
- id: angka dipahat huruf demi huruf dalam kapital roman, di samping gambar kecil seukuran asli, ditahan sendirian

## proof

- en: the finished plate locked: every label and the plate mark in place, the camera only breathing (at most 2%)
- id: pelat jadi terkunci: semua label dan tanda pelat di tempatnya, kamera hanya bernapas pelan

## offer

- en: colour arrives: one transparent wash blooms over the subject from a brush touch while its name is engraved
- id: warna datang: sapuan cat air transparan mekar di atas subjek dari sentuhan kuas, sementara namanya dipahat

## cta

- en: the hand-coloured plate, name and season engraved in the margin, contact on a torn paper slip; held 2 s
- id: pelat berwarna tangan, nama dan musim dipahat di margin, kontak di secarik kertas bertepi sobek; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: pull back to the whole plate as the washes dry; title, roundel and labels locked; held 2 s
- id: kamera mundur ke seluruh pelat saat cat air mengering; judul, lingkaran, dan label terkunci; diam 2 detik
